content.title: When was last time we were on moon? Artemis launch scheduled for this week
content.text: March 30, 2026, 2:51 p.m. ETThe Artemis II mission is to send a crew of four astronauts on a historic 10-day mission around the moon.How long has it been since the last American . astronaut landed on the moon?Why is the Artemis II mission considered "historic"?In some respects, it doesn't seem that long ago.It's been 65 years — within the lifetime of many on Earth today — since men first sat on top of a rocket and launched into space.➤ When is Artemis 2 lifting off? Launch date window, times, what to knowSince then, we've touched the moon, "walked" in space, sent equipment into interstellar space and dream of moving to Mars.As excitement builds for the possible launch this week of Artemis II in a historic manned orbit around the moon, here's both a look back and a glimpse at what could be ahead.What is Artemis II?The Artemis II mission is to send a crew of four astronauts on a historic 10-day mission around the moon.Moon base? What is the mission of the Artemis lunar program?Established during President Donald Trump's first term, NASA's Artemis lunar program is the space agency's campaign to return American astronauts to the surface of the moon for the first time since the Apollo era ended in 1972.➤ NASA unveils $20 billion moon baseNASA's ultimate objective is to use a series of both uncrewed and human lunar landings to set up a permanent moon base at the moon's south pole.A total of $20 billion has been slated for development over the next seven years.When will Artemis II launch from Florida's Cape Canaveral?NASA is planning on an April 1 launch of the Artemis II mission from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, with a two-hour launch window opening at 6:24 p.m. ET. Why is the Artemis II mission considered 'historic'?The astronauts will travel farther from Earth than any human has ever been in space.They're expected to break the Apollo 13 record for farthest distance any human has flown from Earth (248,655 miles).They'll be 6,000 miles above the lunar surface, and will see parts of the far side of the moon that not even Apollo astronauts saw.Who are the astronauts on Artemis II?The Artemis II crew is made up of:Reid Wiseman, commanderVictor Glover, pilotChristina Koch, mission specialistCanadian Space Agency's Jeremy Hansen, mission specialistWhen was the last time an American was on the moon?The last U.S. astronaut to land on the moon was on Dec. 19, 1972, during NASA's Apollo 17 mission. NASA astronauts went to the moon on six separate Apollo missions, beginning with Apollo 11 in 1969.Timeline of human spaceflightApril 12, 1961: Soviets send the first person into space, prompting President John F. Kennedy to say that before the decade ended, the U.S. would land a man on the moon and return him safely to earth.1961-1963, Project Mercury: Project Mercury was the first U.S. program to put humans in space. It made 25 flights, six of which carried astronauts between 1961 and 1963. The objectives of the program were: to orbit a human spacecraft around Earth, to investigate a person’s ability to function in space, and to recover both the astronaut and spacecraft safely.1961: Alan Shepard becomes the first American in space (suborbital).1962: John Glenn becomes the first American in orbit.1965-1966, Gemini Program: The Gemini program's main goals were: to test an astronaut’s ability to fly long duration flights (14 days); to understand how a spacecraft could rendezvous and dock with another vehicle in Earth orbit; to perfect re-entry landing methods; and to further understand the effects of longer spaceflights on astronauts. 1968-1972, Apollo Program: Under the Apollo program, astronauts landed on the moon. The Apollo program also developed technology to meet other national interests in space, conducted scientific exploration of the Moon, and developed humanity’s capability to work in the lunar environment.July 20, 1969, astronaut Neil Armstrong becomes the first person to step onto the moon's surface.1973, Skylab: In 1973, Skylab expeditions paved the way for the International Space Station. The four, windmill-like solar arrays were attached to the Apollo Telescope Mount. Observations of the sun were one of this space lab program’s primary achievements.1981-2011, Space shuttles: NASA's space shuttle fleet — Columbia, Challenger, Discovery, Atlantis and Endeavour — flew 135 missions and carried 355 different people to space. The first reusable spacecraft, the space shuttle carried people into orbit repeatedly; launched, recovered and repaired satellites; conducted cutting-edge research; and built the largest structure in space, the International Space Station.International Space Station: Built between 1998 and 2011, the space station has housed humans continuously since Nov. 2, 2000.2020: SpaceX launches NASA astronauts, beginning the commercial crew era.Lives lost as humans push boundaries into spaceGoing into space is not without risk and Americans have lost their lives. On Jan. 27, 1967, fire swept through the Apollo 1 command module during a preflight test on the Cape Kennedy launch pad. Astronauts Gus Grissom, Ed White, and Roger Chaffee lost their lives. NASA lost two crews of seven in the 1986 Challenger accident and the 2003 Columbia accident.When was the last time Americans were on the moon?Apollo 17 was the sixth and final Apollo mission to land people on the moon. Astronauts with Apollo 17 traveled the greatest distance using the Lunar Roving Vehicle and brought back the greatest number of rock and soil samples. It was the only Apollo mission to carry a trained geologist, Harrison H. Schmitt, and "one of the more notable moments of the Apollo 17 mission happened when Schmitt discovered orange soil."Artemis missions to launch from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, FloridaAll of NASA's Artemis missions will get off the ground from the Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, located along Florida's Atlantic coast.Moon landing planned for 2028. What to know about Artemis 3, 4A moon landing is now due to take place as early as 2028 during a mission known as Artemis IV.Prior to that mission, Artemis III astronauts aboard the Orion capsule are due to meet and dock in 2027 in Earth orbit with at least one of the commercial lunar landers being developed by Elon Musk's SpaceX and Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin.NASA will also use the mission to test space suits, known as extravehicular activity suits, being developed by Axiom Space for astronauts on the lunar surface.After the Artemis 5 mission, NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman has said the agency wants to target a human lunar landing up to twice a year – if not more often.Get the latest space news, launch informationFor the latest news from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station and NASA's Kennedy Space Center, visit floridatoday.com/space. Cheryl McCloud is a journalist for the USA TODAY Network-Florida's service journalism Connect team.
